title: CBAP/CCBA Certified Business Analysis prep test 2025

questions.question: A business analyst is using the 'MoSCoW' prioritization technique. Which of the following BEST describes the ‘Should Have’ category?
answers: Requirements that must be included in the solution for it to be considered a success.
Requirements that are very desirable, but not essential for the success of the solution.
Requirements that are important to have, but not critical, for the solution to function correctly.
Requirements that will not be included in the solution for this project.
feedbacks: This describes ‘Must Have’ requirements.
This describes ‘Could Have’ requirements.
This is the best definition of the ‘Should Have’ category.
This describes the ‘Won't Have this time’ requirements.
questions.explanation: Should Have requirements are important and valuable, but the solution can still be deployed and meet all of its core objectives without these requirements.

questions.question: A business analyst is working with a project team that has very limited time and resources, but they still want to deliver maximum value to the organization. Which action is MOST likely to deliver the best results?
answers: Include all the requirements in the project, as this will deliver the most value.
Focus solely on the technical requirements, and ignore the needs of the business users.
Prioritize requirements based on their business value, and focus on the most important requirements first.
Remove any non functional requirements, and focus solely on delivering core functionality.
feedbacks: This approach may mean that the project goes over time, and may lead to scope creep.
This approach will not provide business value.
This approach is ideal for limited resources.
This may mean that the system is not usable, and will lack value.
questions.explanation: Prioritizing requirements by business value means that the project team is focusing on the things that will deliver the most benefit to the organization, while still being realistic with limited resources.

questions.question: A business analyst has just finished gathering all the requirements for a project. Which action is MOST important for the business analyst to take before the project can move to the design phase?
answers: Start documenting all of the requirements in a standard format, so that they are easier to read.
Immediately provide the requirements to the development team, so that they can start the design process.
Analyze, review, and validate all of the requirements with the stakeholders to ensure they are clear and accurate.
Create a long list of risks, and ensure these are managed correctly by the project manager.
feedbacks: Documentation is important, but should be done after analysis and validation.
Requirements should always be validated with stakeholders, before going to the development team.
This is key to making sure requirements are correct, and have stakeholder buy in.
This is part of risk management, and not part of requirements validation.
questions.explanation: Analyzing, reviewing, and validating requirements with stakeholders is key to making sure that the requirements are complete, accurate and have stakeholder buy-in.

questions.question: A business analyst is documenting a process, and they need to show where different paths might be taken based on certain conditions. Which symbol would BEST represent this?
answers: A circle.
A rectangle.
A square.
A diamond.
feedbacks: This represents an event.
This represents an action.
This represents a data store.
This represents a decision.
questions.explanation: A diamond is used in process models to represent a decision point, where the process flow can branch into different paths, based on conditions or rules.

questions.question: A business analyst is working on a project where a key stakeholder is consistently providing vague and high level requirements. What approach should the business analyst use to gather more detail?
answers: Document the high level requirements, and proceed with the rest of the requirements.
Remove the stakeholder from the project as their input is not valuable.
Ask clarifying questions, and ask for specific examples to understand the requirements in more detail.
Ignore the requirements from this stakeholder, and focus on the other stakeholder requirements.
feedbacks: This will lead to incomplete requirements, and is not ideal.
This approach is not collaborative.
This is the best approach to get more information.
This may lead to key things being missed, and is not collaborative.
questions.explanation: By asking clarifying questions, and asking for specific examples, the business analyst can gather a more detailed understanding of the requirements, and have a clearer picture of what is required.

questions.question: A business analyst is using 'prototyping' as an approach for gathering requirements. Which of the following is the MOST important reason to use this technique?
answers: To document all of the requirements in a detailed written document.
To create a fully functional system that is ready for immediate deployment.
To allow stakeholders to interact with a preliminary version of the system and provide feedback.
To define the technical architecture and design of the system.
feedbacks: Prototypes are not used for documentation, but to gather feedback.
Prototypes are not for deployment, they are to gather information.
This is the key reason why prototypes are used.
This is not the purpose of prototyping.
questions.explanation: A prototype allows stakeholders to get hands on experience with the proposed system and provide feedback that will help to refine the requirements and the design.

questions.question: A business analyst is responsible for ensuring that all the stakeholders for a project understand the scope of the project. Which of the following is the BEST approach to ensure this?
answers: Share a detailed document that lists all of the project tasks with all the stakeholders.
Conduct a detailed technical review of the project, with all stakeholders.
Document and share a clear, and concise project scope statement with all stakeholders.
Send all of the stakeholders a link to the project repository, and ask them to review all the requirements.
feedbacks: This does not define the scope of the project.
This is not suitable for a non-technical audience.
This is the best approach for scope management.
This will not allow the stakeholders to fully understand the overall scope of the project.
questions.explanation: A clear and concise scope statement will define what is included, and excluded from the project, and helps to align all stakeholders to the agreed scope of the project.

questions.question: A business analyst has identified several high-priority risks for a project. Which action is MOST important for the business analyst to take in managing these risks?
answers: Ignore the risks as most of the risks will probably never happen.
Document the risks and escalate them to the project manager.
Create detailed risk mitigation plans, and actively monitor these throughout the project.
Document the risks in a register, but do not worry about these as risks are part of every project.
feedbacks: Ignoring risks is never a good strategy and may cause problems.
This is a reactive approach, and the BA should be more proactive.
This is the best approach, as it is proactive and prevents issues.
This is not ideal as this will not mitigate risks.
questions.explanation: Detailed mitigation plans that are monitored, help to prevent risks, and ensures the project can deliver its objectives without being derailed.

questions.question: A business analyst is using a ‘data flow diagram’. Which of the following is represented by a rectangle in a data flow diagram?
answers: A data store where data is held.
A flow of data from one place to another.
An external entity that sends or receives data.
A process or activity that manipulates or changes data.
feedbacks: This is represented by a square.
This is represented by an arrow.
This is represented by a rounded rectangle.
This is represented by a rectangle.
questions.explanation: A rectangle in a data flow diagram represents a process or action that is performed on the data as it flows through the system.

questions.question: A business analyst is trying to manage a project where the scope is constantly changing. Which approach is BEST suited to ensure the project is able to deliver the most value in this type of environment?
answers: Adhere to the original requirements, and do not accept any change requests.
Document all changes, but continue working with the original project scope.
Adopt an agile approach, that embraces change, and allows for the frequent review of the project scope.
Use a very strict change management process, to limit the number of changes to the project scope.
feedbacks: This will lead to an outdated solution and unhappy stakeholders.
This will not be agile, and will cause misalignment.
This approach is ideal for constantly changing requirements.
This approach limits the ability to adapt to change and may lead to an outdated product.
questions.explanation: An agile approach with iterative planning allows the project to be flexible, and to adapt to changing requirements, while always focusing on delivering maximum business value.

questions.question: A business analyst is using a 'use case narrative' to document a functional requirement. What is MOST likely to be documented in the use case narrative?
answers: The detailed technical specifications for developing the user interface.
The security requirements of the system, such as authentication and data protection.
A description of the steps that the user takes when using the system, to complete a specific task.
The data structure, and how the data is stored in the system.
feedbacks: This is part of the user interface design, not a use case.
This is a non functional requirement and not part of a use case narrative.
This is the main purpose of the use case narrative.
This is documented as part of data modeling.
questions.explanation: A use case narrative documents the flow of actions that a user completes when using the system to achieve a specific task.

questions.question: A business analyst is working on a project, and needs to validate that a developed solution meets all the requirements. What is the MOST important action that the business analyst must take?
answers: Ensure the solution has been developed according to the technical specifications.
Conduct testing to ensure that the solution performs as expected under load.
Engage the stakeholders, and confirm that the solution meets their needs and expectations.
Document all the issues, and create a list of enhancements for the next project.
feedbacks: This is part of technical design validation and not solution validation.
This is part of system testing and not solution validation.
This approach is key to making sure that the solution is fit for purpose.
This is not ideal, as the project must meet the requirements of the stakeholders before being completed.
questions.explanation: Solution validation is focussed on ensuring that the developed solution meets the documented needs of the stakeholders and business, and is fit for purpose.

questions.question: A business analyst is working with a group of stakeholders, and they need to facilitate a session where all stakeholders are able to participate equally, and all views are heard. What is the BEST way to manage the session?
answers: Ensure that the most senior stakeholders are given more time to express their views.
Allow each stakeholder to present their ideas, without any interruptions from other stakeholders.
Create a structured discussion format, so that each stakeholder has an equal opportunity to participate and share their views.
Let the stakeholders debate the various ideas, without any intervention from the business analyst, as this will make for more creative discussion.
feedbacks: This will cause a lack of engagement from the other stakeholders.
This is not a collaborative approach and will not allow any debate or discussion.
This is the best approach for collaborative discussion.
This will likely lead to conflict and a lack of a structured outcome.
questions.explanation: A structured discussion ensures all stakeholders are heard, and it allows a productive environment where all viewpoints can be shared, discussed and a consensus can be reached.

questions.question: A business analyst is working on a project and needs to identify different types of users of the system, and their respective roles. Which of the following approaches is BEST suited to achieve this?
answers: Create a use case diagram that shows how the users interact with the system.
Use data modeling to capture the different types of data that each user will access.
Conduct a stakeholder analysis, and classify the users based on their roles and responsibilities.
Use process mapping, to map all the processes that will be used by the users.
feedbacks: This shows the interaction and not necessarily the different user types.
This will only capture the data requirements and not the user types.
This is the best approach to understand the different user types.
This will not identify the different user types.
questions.explanation: Stakeholder analysis is the ideal approach to identify all stakeholders, their roles, responsibilities and influence in the project.

questions.question: A business analyst is using a ‘5 Whys’ approach, and they have asked why several times, and they keep returning to the same point. What is the MOST effective next step for the business analyst to take?
answers: Assume they have found the root cause and proceed to the next step.
Stop the 5 Whys analysis and ask the project manager for guidance.
Review the line of questioning, and determine if the questions should be re-phrased to take a new approach.
Document the current findings, and continue with the project, since they cannot find any more information.
feedbacks: This may be incorrect as it has not been fully explored.
This is a reactive approach. The BA should first try to resolve the issue.
This may help to explore other root causes.
This is not ideal and may lead to a sub-optimal solution.
questions.explanation: By reviewing and changing the questions, the BA may be able to uncover new information that helps identify the root cause, and this is essential for a good outcome.

questions.question: A business analyst is responsible for defining non-functional requirements for a new system. Which of the following would be considered a ‘performance’ requirement?
answers: The system must be available for a minimum of 99.9% of the time.
The system must have a user interface that is easy to navigate and use.
The system must process 1000 transactions per second during peak times.
The system must protect all sensitive data using encryption and authentication.
feedbacks: This is an availability requirement and not a performance requirement.
This is a usability requirement and not a performance requirement.
This is a performance requirement.
This is a security requirement and not a performance requirement.
questions.explanation: Performance requirements are focussed on the systems responsiveness, throughput, speed and scalability.

questions.question: A business analyst is working with a set of stakeholders and there are multiple conflicting requirements, with no easy way to resolve them. What should the business analyst do to move the project forward?
answers: Prioritize the requirements based on which requirements are easiest to implement first.
Escalate all of the conflicting requirements to the project manager and ask them to make a decision.
Document all the conflicting requirements and proceed to the next phase without resolving the issues.
Facilitate a series of meetings where stakeholders can discuss the requirements, and try to find common ground and compromise.
feedbacks: This is not an ideal approach and does not consider business value.
This is a reactive approach, and not a good approach.
This will create problems in the future as requirements will not be aligned.
This approach will lead to better outcomes by discussing and trying to resolve issues.
questions.explanation: Facilitating discussion between stakeholders will allow for compromise and is key to resolving conflicts in an open and collaborative manner.

questions.question: A business analyst has completed gathering and documenting all of the requirements for a project. What is the MOST important action that the business analyst should take at this point?
answers: Immediately hand all the requirements over to the development team, and start the design phase.
Start testing the requirements, to ensure they meet the required test criteria.
Prioritize all of the requirements based on the business value and complexity of implementation.
Review, analyze, and validate all requirements with all stakeholders, to ensure they are all accurate and complete.
feedbacks: This is not ideal and the requirements must be validated.
This is not validation, and is more about test planning.
Prioritization should have been done during the analysis and not after the analysis.
This is the most important step, to make sure requirements are valid.
questions.explanation: Analyzing, reviewing and validating with the stakeholders is critical before moving to the next phase of the project. It ensures that the requirements are complete, correct, and have stakeholder agreement.

questions.question: Which of the following is MOST likely to be included in a 'data dictionary'?
answers: The diagram of all the different user types, and how they will interact with the system.
The definition, format, and data types of all the data elements that are stored in the system.
The business rules and constraints that govern the different processes in the system.
The graphical user interfaces and the layouts of the various screens in the system.
feedbacks: This is part of the user interaction, and not the data dictionary.
This is the key purpose of a data dictionary.
This is part of the business rules, and not the data dictionary.
This is part of user interface design and not the data dictionary.
questions.explanation: A data dictionary describes the data that is stored in a system including its name, data type, format, and any constraints.

questions.question: A business analyst is working on a project with a key stakeholder that has a lot of influence, but they are not very interested in the project. What is the best approach to manage this stakeholder?
answers: Ignore this stakeholder, and focus on the stakeholders who are engaged in the project.
Keep them fully informed about the project, and actively engage them in all the project activities.
Make an effort to keep them satisfied, and make sure they are not creating any resistance to the project.
Minimize communication with this stakeholder, as they are not interested in the project.
feedbacks: This is not advisable, as their influence is key to the project's success.
This approach may be ineffective, as the stakeholders are not interested in the project.
This will ensure that their lack of interest does not negatively impact the project.
This will not work as the stakeholder may object later as they are not engaged.
questions.explanation: A high-influence, low-interest stakeholder must be kept satisfied to avoid any negative impact.

questions.question: A business analyst is facilitating a session with a set of stakeholders, and they are using a 'use case diagram'. Which element is used to represent a system function or interaction?
answers: An association
A boundary
An actor
A use case
feedbacks: This is used to show the relationship between an actor and a use case.
This is used to show the scope of the system.
This is an external entity that interacts with the system.
This is a specific interaction with the system.
questions.explanation: A use case represents an interaction or a function that the system can perform.

questions.question: A business analyst has identified several risks on their project, and they are now in the 'Planning' phase. What is the most important action for the business analyst to take?
answers: Ignore the risks as many risks are unlikely to occur anyway.
Document the risks, and escalate to the project manager to manage.
Develop risk mitigation strategies for the highest priority risks, and monitor them.
Document the risks in a register and move on with the next steps.
feedbacks: This is not a good strategy. Risks must be managed proactively.
This is not proactive, and is a reactive approach.
This is the best approach to take, and helps minimize the impact of the risks.
This will not help mitigate the risks or minimize their impact.
questions.explanation: Developing risk mitigation strategies and monitoring them throughout the project helps to prevent, or minimize the impact of any negative risks.

questions.question: A business analyst is working on a project where the requirements are constantly changing. What is the best approach to manage requirements?
answers: Document the initial set of requirements and then refuse to make any changes to the scope.
Use a waterfall approach to the project, as this method is very good for project control.
Adopt an agile approach and prioritize flexibility, and respond to change on an iterative basis.
Document all changes to requirements, but do not implement any of the changes in the project.
feedbacks: This will lead to an outdated solution and disengaged stakeholders.
Waterfall approaches do not allow flexibility.
This approach is ideal for managing change, and ensures business value.
This will cause misalignment with the business.
questions.explanation: Agile methodologies are designed to be responsive to change and allows projects to adapt to changing requirements, and changing business needs.

questions.question: A business analyst is responsible for the 'solution validation' phase of the project. What is the primary goal of this phase?
answers: To ensure that all the technical aspects of the solution have been implemented correctly.
To ensure that the solution has been designed according to the business requirements.
To ensure that the solution meets the needs of the stakeholders and provides the required business value.
To ensure the solution performs as expected under realistic load conditions.
feedbacks: This is the purpose of code reviews.
This is part of the design process.
This is the core goal of solution validation.
This is part of testing, and not the solution validation.
questions.explanation: Solution validation is focused on ensuring that the solution delivers the required value and that it meets all the business requirements and stakeholder needs.

questions.question: A business analyst is working with a group of stakeholders and needs to prioritize a large number of requirements. Which of the following would be BEST to manage this?
answers: Use a simple list of all the requirements, without any prioritization.
Prioritize the requirements based on which ones are the easiest to implement.
Prioritize the requirements based on stakeholder influence and power in the organization.
Use a prioritization technique, such as MoSCoW, to categorize the requirements based on their business value.
feedbacks: This is not an effective approach to manage a large list of requirements.
This is not ideal as it does not consider business value.
This is not an ideal approach to prioritization.
This is the ideal approach for prioritizing requirements.
questions.explanation: Prioritizing the requirements based on value using a method such as MoSCoW will allow the project team to focus on delivering the highest value items first.

questions.question: Which of the following is MOST likely to be included in a 'stakeholder analysis'?
answers: The steps the user will take to use the system.
The detailed technical design of the system and its components.
The identification, assessment, and classification of stakeholders based on their interest and influence.
The requirements that are needed for the system to meet the needs of the users.
feedbacks: This is part of the use case and not stakeholder analysis.
This is part of the system design, and not stakeholder analysis.
This is the key purpose of stakeholder analysis.
This is part of the requirements process, and not stakeholder analysis.
questions.explanation: Stakeholder analysis allows the business analyst to identify and classify the project stakeholders, based on their influence, interest and impact on the project.

questions.question: A business analyst is using the '5 Whys' technique to find the root cause of a problem. They keep asking why, but are still unable to get to the core of the problem. What is the best approach to take?
answers: Assume that the root cause is not discoverable and move on.
Stop the 5 Whys analysis, and escalate the problem to the project manager.
Re-evaluate the 5 Whys questions, and change the line of questioning to explore alternative avenues.
Assume that there is more than one root cause, and pick the easiest one to resolve.
feedbacks: This will leave the problem unresolved, and may cause issues in the future.
This is not a good approach, and does not allow the BA to actively look for a solution.
This approach allows the BA to change direction and potentially uncover new causes.
This may not resolve the true issue, and may lead to a sub-optimal outcome.
questions.explanation: Re-evaluating the questions and rephrasing them can help the business analyst to explore alternative avenues, and to potentially get to the core cause of the issue.

questions.question: A business analyst is working on a project and is responsible for documenting the non-functional requirements for the system. Which of the following would be considered a 'security' requirement?
answers: The system must have a response time of under 1 second for all key actions.
The system must be easy to use and navigate, and must be accessible to all users.
The system must use encryption to protect all sensitive data, both at rest and in transit.
The system must be available for a minimum of 99.9% of the time, to ensure reliability.
feedbacks: This is a performance requirement and not a security requirement.
This is a usability and accessibility requirement, not security.
This is a security requirement.
This is an availability requirement and not security.
questions.explanation: Security requirements are focussed on protecting all data and preventing unauthorized access, and include data encryption, authentication and authorization.

questions.question: A business analyst is managing a project where the stakeholders have different opinions on the project’s requirements. What approach should the business analyst take FIRST to resolve this issue?
answers: Document all of the differing opinions and proceed with the rest of the project.
Prioritize the requirements based on the opinion of the senior stakeholders.
Ignore the conflicting requirements and choose the requirements that the business analyst thinks are the best.
Facilitate a structured discussion with all stakeholders, to understand their viewpoints and find a suitable consensus.
feedbacks: This approach ignores the issue and will cause more problems.
This will disengage other stakeholders and is not a collaborative approach.
This will not solve the problem and may lead to misalignment.
This is the best approach as it allows for discussion and the finding of solutions.
questions.explanation: Facilitating a structured discussion allows all stakeholders to share their opinions, and helps the project team to work towards resolving the issues, and finding a common ground.

questions.question: A business analyst has just finished the analysis phase of a project and they are moving to the next phase. Which action is MOST important for them to take before they start the next phase?
answers: Present all of the requirements to the technical team, to allow them to begin the design phase of the project.
Begin creating the test plans, so that the technical team are able to fully test the system when it is developed.
Analyze, review, and validate all of the requirements with the stakeholders, to ensure they are complete, correct and accurate.
Prioritize all of the requirements, so that the technical team know which requirements they must focus on first.
feedbacks: The requirements should always be validated before being given to the technical team.
Test planning is done later in the project.
This is a key step, prior to the next phase of the project.
Prioritization should occur prior to the analysis phase, and not after the analysis phase.
questions.explanation: Reviewing, analyzing and validating all of the requirements with stakeholders will make sure that there are no errors or conflicts, and that the requirements are ready for the next phase of the project.

questions.question: A business analyst is using a ‘use case diagram’ to document how a user will interact with a system. Which of the following elements represents a user or an external system that interacts with the system?
answers: A use case.
An association.
A system boundary.
An actor.
feedbacks: This is the interaction or the function that the system can perform.
This is the line connecting the user and the use case.
This represents the scope of the system.
This represents a user or external entity.
questions.explanation: An actor is an external user or system that interacts with the system.

questions.question: Which of the following is MOST likely to be documented in a 'business rules' document?
answers: The detailed steps that a user must follow to complete a specific task.
The rules and constraints that define how the organization operates.
The various user interfaces that are used by users to interact with the system.
The database structure, and the data elements that will be stored by the system.
feedbacks: This is documented in a use case.
This is the main purpose of a business rule document.
This is part of UI design, and not business rules.
This is part of data modeling and not business rules.
questions.explanation: Business rules are a description of how the organization operates, and includes policies, constraints, and guidelines that govern business operations.

questions.question: A business analyst is facilitating a workshop and the stakeholders are having trouble understanding some of the proposed concepts. What is the MOST effective approach for the business analyst to take?
answers: Use highly technical jargon, to ensure all of the concepts are fully explained.
Continue with the presentation, without trying to simplify the concepts.
Present the concepts in plain language, avoiding any jargon, and provide examples of how they work.
Document all the proposed concepts, and ask the stakeholders to review this after the workshop.
feedbacks: Technical jargon will make things worse and cause more confusion.
This is not ideal and may lose the stakeholders.
This is the best approach and allows all stakeholders to understand the concepts.
This approach is not collaborative, and will not resolve the lack of understanding.
questions.explanation: Using plain language, avoiding jargon, and providing examples will allow the stakeholders to fully understand the concepts being presented.

questions.question: A business analyst is using 'prototyping' to gather requirements for a project. Which is the MOST important thing to ensure for the prototype to be successful?
answers: That the prototype looks and feels exactly like the finished product.
That the prototype has all the functionality of the required system, for a complete user experience.
That the prototype demonstrates the core functionality, and allows users to interact with the key parts of the system.
That all of the documentation for the system has been completed before the prototype is used.
feedbacks: This is not the purpose of a prototype, which is designed to get early feedback.
A prototype is not a complete system, and will not have all the functionality.
This is key to ensure that the prototype is fit for purpose.
Documentation is not the purpose of the prototype.
questions.explanation: The main objective of prototyping is to allow users to interact with the core functionality and to provide feedback on the key aspects of the system.

questions.question: A business analyst is working on a project where the requirements are not fully defined, but the project has a very strict timeline. What is the BEST action for the business analyst to take?
answers: Focus on gathering all of the requirements before starting any design work.
Create a detailed design document for the system, and assume that the requirements are complete.
Use an iterative agile approach, focusing on the core requirements and iterate as the project progresses.
Document the initial set of requirements, and refuse any further change requests.
feedbacks: This is not ideal given the time constraints.
This approach may not meet the business needs and expectations.
This is the best way to work in a project with an unknown scope.
This is not ideal for a changing project, and it may disengage stakeholders.
questions.explanation: An agile approach allows the project to be iterative, and will allow for flexibility, and to respond to changes in requirements as the project evolves.

questions.question: A business analyst is using a ‘data flow diagram’. Which of the following elements represents a storage location of data in the diagram?
answers: A diamond
A rectangle
A circle
A cylinder or a square.
feedbacks: This represents a decision.
This represents an activity or task.
This represents an event.
This represents a data store.
questions.explanation: A square or a cylinder is used in a data flow diagram to represent where data is stored or persisted.

questions.question: A business analyst has identified several significant risks to a project during the planning phase. What is the MOST important action for the business analyst to take?
answers: Escalate the risks to the project manager and ask them to manage the risks.
Document the risks, and proceed with the project, since most risks are unlikely to occur.
Prioritize the risks based on their potential impact, and create mitigation plans for the highest priority risks.
Remove all high priority risks from the project, to ensure that the project does not fail.
feedbacks: This is a reactive approach, and is not recommended.
This is not proactive and risks must be managed.
This approach allows for proactive risk management.
This approach may lead to key things being missed.
questions.explanation: Risk mitigation is key to reducing the impact of potential problems, and a prioritized list of risks, with mitigation plans, will ensure that the project is not derailed by issues.

questions.question: A business analyst is using a ‘use case diagram’. Which of the following would be represented by a stick figure?
answers: A use case.
A boundary.
An actor.
An association.
feedbacks: This is a function that the system performs.
This represents the scope of the system.
This represents a user or external system.
This is the relationship between an actor and a use case.
questions.explanation: An actor represents a user or external system that interacts with the system.

questions.question: A business analyst is working with a key stakeholder, and they are constantly requesting changes to the requirements. What is the BEST way to manage this?
answers: Refuse to accept any further changes from this stakeholder, and proceed with the project.
Document all of the changes, and continue with the project as per the original requirements.
Work with the stakeholder, to prioritize the requested changes, and manage them using a defined change process.
Ignore the stakeholder, and assume that the most current requirements are the correct ones.
feedbacks: This approach will cause issues with stakeholder engagement, and is not advised.
This approach will lead to issues later in the project and will not deliver what the stakeholders need.
This is the best approach, and will allow the project to remain flexible.
This is not a collaborative approach and will lead to poor stakeholder engagement.
questions.explanation: Using a change management process will allow the business analyst to manage change requests in a structured and controlled way and ensures the project can remain flexible, and deliver value.

questions.question: A business analyst is working with a group of stakeholders, and they are having trouble coming to an agreement on the scope of the project. What is the BEST approach for the business analyst to take first?
answers: Prioritize the requirements, based on the input of the most senior stakeholders.
Define the scope of the project, based on their own opinions, and proceed with the project.
Document all the differing opinions, and proceed with the project, and ignore any concerns.
Facilitate a workshop where all stakeholders can openly discuss the project scope, and work towards a common understanding.
feedbacks: This will disengage the other stakeholders, and may lead to poor outcomes.
This is not a collaborative approach, and will likely lead to poor results.
This will cause issues later in the project and will not lead to a positive outcome.
This is the best approach, as it allows collaboration and discussion.
questions.explanation: Facilitating a workshop will help the stakeholders to have an open discussion and to understand the differing opinions. This helps to define the scope and come to an agreement that is supported by the stakeholders.

questions.question: A business analyst is working on a new project, and they need to understand the current workflows that are being used in the organization. What is the BEST approach to document the current processes?
answers: Data modeling
Use case modeling

This approach is reactive, and the BA needs to proactively address the issues.
