To graphically represent and analyze the flow of activities within a business process.
To capture the requirements for a user interface.
To define the data structure and relationships for a system.
feedbacks: This is part of design documentation.
This accurately describes the use of business process models.
This is done using user interface designs.
This is done using data modeling.
questions.explanation: A process model is used to document and represent the flow of all activities in a process, as well as all decision points and events.

questions.question: A business analyst is using 'prototyping' as a method of eliciting requirements for a new system. Which of the following BEST describes why this approach is used?
answers: To document the final technical specifications of the new system.
To create a fully working system, that can be put into production without needing any further work.
To allow the stakeholders to interact with a preliminary version of the system, and to provide feedback.
To provide complete requirements documentation so that there are no gaps.
feedbacks: This is the purpose of the design specifications.
This is not the goal of prototyping, which focuses on early feedback.
This is the main benefit of the prototyping approach.
This is not the purpose of prototyping. It is more focused on exploring the requirements.
questions.explanation: Prototypes provide a tangible way for stakeholders to explore, interact with, and provide feedback on, the solution.

questions.question: A business analyst has identified a large number of risks to their project, which action is MOST important for the business analyst to take to manage the risks?
answers: Ignore the risks since they are unlikely to all happen, and proceed with the project.
Document all the risks in a risk register, and do not focus on them.
Develop mitigation plans for the key risks, and monitor them on an ongoing basis.
Escalate the risks to the project manager, and allow them to manage the risks.
feedbacks: This is not ideal, as risks must be managed proactively.
This does not allow any mitigation actions to take place.
This allows for a proactive management of the risks.
This is a reactive approach. The BA should be proactive.
questions.explanation: Mitigating and monitoring key risks on an ongoing basis is critical to the success of the project.

questions.question: A business analyst is working on a project where the stakeholders are constantly requesting scope changes. What is the BEST approach to manage these scope changes?
answers: Document all the change requests, but continue with the project using the original requirements.
Ignore the changes as it is important to adhere to the original plan for the project.
Assess the impacts of all the changes, and use a change management process to control all changes.
Decline all change requests to avoid any impact on the project timeline.
feedbacks: This is not ideal and ignores the stakeholder needs.
This approach is not agile, and may cause stakeholder disengagement.
This is the best approach as it allows the BA to assess, control and manage change.
This is not collaborative and may disengage stakeholders.
questions.explanation: A change management approach is key to assess, control and implement change requests, and to ensure that scope creep is controlled and managed correctly.

questions.question: A business analyst is responsible for the 'solution validation' phase of a project. Which action is MOST important for the business analyst to undertake during this phase?
answers: Analyze the code written by the development team to ensure the quality is high.
Verify that the solution meets all the business requirements and the stakeholders needs.
Test the performance of the system to ensure it meets the response time requirements.
Document all the design elements and the technical requirements of the system.
feedbacks: This is part of a code review, and is not part of solution validation.
This is the core element of the validation process.
This is part of the performance testing and not the validation phase.
This is part of the design documentation.
questions.explanation: Solution validation is focused on ensuring that the solution delivers the required value and that it meets all the requirements and stakeholder needs.
